serp_ownership.read: vendors own the results page — paid acquisition is likely the only door

revenue_estimate.note: No observed price — revenue left unestimated rather than inferred from search volume.

positive_signals: 4 small vendors selling, none funded — demand proven, room to differentiate
negative_signals: vendors own the buyer-intent results page — paid may be the only channel

claude_analysis.tam_assessment: EEGLAB is a niche academic tool with moderate, flat search interest (Google Trends 45), no Hacker News posts, and only 6 Reddit hits, so the market is likely limited to EEG research labs and grad students, estimated at roughly 10,000 potential customers.
claude_analysis.pricing_assessment: No competitor price was observed, so ~$100/yr per lab is an assumption; willingness to pay is likely low because the 4 'incumbents' found (MathWorks File Exchange, eeglab.org, NITRC, numfer) are free distribution channels rather than paid vendors, and academic users expect free open-source tooling.
claude_analysis.legal_reasoning: The regulatory probe found no restriction signals and no government sources, but MathWorks licensing terms may limit bundling full MATLAB in a redistributable container, and the probe did not cover that.
key_risks: Free substitutes are the default: EEGLAB is open source and distributed free via eeglab.org, MathWorks File Exchange and NITRC, and Python/Octave toolchains can replace it
MATLAB licensing may force users to bring their own license, which reduces the value of the container and complicates distribution
Price-sensitive academic buyers, with 40% of search results owned by vendor or official sites, leave little room for organic acquisition
key_opportunities: Steady research demand (flat, moderate Trends interest), plus Reddit r/BCI threads about installation and setup pain
No funded competitor was found, so there is room for a reproducible, preconfigured environment aimed at labs and HPC clusters
Possible expansion into hosted or cloud EEG processing, or OpenBCI hobbyist onboarding
claude_analysis.value_reasoning: About 10,000 potential customers × about $100/yr ≈ $1,000,000 total addressable annual revenue.
claude_analysis.probability_reasoning: Competition is 'contested' so no ceiling applies, but free official distributions and a free-software norm in academia make realistic paid penetration likely well under 1%, which puts this in the moonshot tier.
